first.rationale:
Two of the three current problems are internal funnel declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and the inherited record points at onboarding friction twice (memory_86, memory_31) rather than once. That is the closest match between a known lever and the actual observed deficit, so it is where a single scarce experiment slot buys the most information. I am deliberately not chasing promotional_pricing (memory_73) even though the competitor's entry pricing makes it the emotionally obvious response: discount-driven acquisition is the classic way to book revenue that does not survive contact with renewal, and the stated objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not this quarter's bookings. If I do run pricing later, I would want memory_73's original record first, because its summary says 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' with no retention or margin horizon attached.

I am spending the one verification pull on memory_86 because it is the memory my chosen action leans on hardest and the one whose summary is most abstracted. 'Shortening onboarding improved completion' does not tell me what was shortened, on which segment, over what window, or whether the lift persisted past week one. memory_31 corroborates it, but corroboration between two consolidated summaries is weak evidence — both may descend from the same original test, and both have had their caveats stripped by consolidation. The archived record should tell me whether they are genuinely independent.

The specific downstream risk I want to flag: memory_31's mechanism is 'cutting required fields at signup.' Fields at signup are also qualification and routing data. memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows, which depends on being able to identify an enterprise prospect at signup. So a change that raises SMB activation could simultaneously degrade enterprise routing and lower the qualified share of new revenue — improving the metric while damaging the objective. That is exactly the failure mode the consolidated summaries cannot warn me about, since each was recorded in isolation.

Therefore: small guarded test, not a broad rollout. Hold out a control, instrument lead quality and enterprise-path routing alongside completion rate, and require the qualified-revenue mix to hold flat before any expansion. If verification shows memory_86 was measured only on self-serve SMB over a short window, I treat its applicability to the current mixed-segment decline as unproven and keep the test correspondingly narrow.

final.rationale:
Verification strengthened memory_86 in the way that matters most: exp_86 reports 30-day retention +3% alongside completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days. That is a durability signal, not just a funnel-metric bump, which is exactly the evidence the objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) requires. Confirmed conclusion, real horizon attached. I commit the slot to simplify_onboarding.

But the pull also sharpened a distinction the consolidated summaries had blurred. exp_86 tested a shortened onboarding flow. memory_31 describes a different mechanism — cutting required fields at signup. Those are not the same intervention, and only the first is now verified. I read this as evidence that memory_86 and memory_31 are probably independent records rather than two summaries of one test, which is mildly reassuring, but it also means the field-cutting variant carries none of the retention evidence I just bought. So I implement the verified version: compress and resequence the onboarding flow, defer non-essential steps, and explicitly preserve the qualification and routing fields at signup. That directly retires the main downstream risk I flagged — memory_44's enterprise sales-assist path depends on identifying enterprise prospects early, and I am no longer touching the data that routing depends on.

Residual uncertainty I am not pretending away: exp_86's segment coverage and baseline conditions are still unknown to me, and it ran against a market without the current competitor's entry pricing. A lift measured in one competitive environment need not transfer to another. The current declines are also only partly explained by onboarding — activation is down 6% against onboarding's 4%, so memory_91's in-product activation messaging remains a live and unspent hypothesis for a later slot. And I am still declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor pressure: memory_73 offers acquisition and revenue lift with no retention horizon at all, which is the profile of a lever that flatters the quarter and erodes the objective. If pricing is revisited, exp_73's original record should be pulled first.

Guardrails on execution: hold out a randomized control, instrument enterprise-path routing volume and qualified-lead share alongside completion and activation, and require the qualified-revenue mix to hold flat or improve before any expansion beyond the test cell. Confirmed-and-durable is a reason to proceed at guarded scale, not a licence to skip the control.
